summary: Support leads change answers and routing rules themselves through an admin page with version history, undo and automatic checks. Failed lookups are captured with their area. No AI. A backup command exists, but nothing tests a restore.

archetype.reason: A help desk for one company, not a platform for building others.

persistent_data.reason: SQLite database of users, definitions, settings and failed lookups.

multi_tenant.reason: One company runs one Rules Desk; no organisation or workspace in the data model.

machine_actions.reason: A token-authenticated JSON admin API changes answers, rules and settings.

evolution_auto_apply.reason: No evolution loop; people make every change.

definition_change_path.reason: Answers and rules are versioned definitions changed at runtime.

code_release_path.reason: No evolution system or AI writes code.

ai_features.reason: 'Smart matching' is keyword overlap and regular expressions, not a model.

MAL-10.reason: Routing rules are data (pattern, queue, priority) composed by leads with a try mode; narrow in scope, so 2 or 3.

MAL-20.reason: The help widget is a keyword bot, the anchor for 1.

DEL-01.reason: Change requests arrive by email outside the product.

DEL-05.reason: CI runs on every pull request and answers and rules are checked before going live, but settings changes have no check.

DEL-06.reason: Health endpoint with a version; no configuration snapshot.

ARC-02.reason: Numbered forward-only migrations applied by a command; no down steps.

ARC-09.reason: A documented backup command; the only test checks that a file is written, and no restore exists or is tested.

LRN-02.reason: Failed lookups are typed records but not linked to the definition and version they concern.

LRN-03.reason: Failed lookups are recorded with area and channel and queryable by area.

LRN-05.reason: No grouping or diagnosis; leads read a raw list.

LRN-07.reason: Leads turn failed lookups into answers by hand at most.

LRN-08.reason: No learned or AI-made changes; a rater may score 0, or 2 for the checks any rule change would pass. Two readings under the boundary.

LRN-10.reason: Checks are fixed in code and change only when engineers edit them.

EXP-04.reason: Unanswered questions are recorded in queryable form, the anchor for 2.

GOV-02.reason: Definition versions record the author; settings and other changes are not audited.

GOV-05.reason: Answers and rules have history and undo, but greeting and opening hours are overwritten with no history, despite the README's 'every admin change can be undone'.

GOV-06.reason: Changes go live on save; the only proposal path is code pull requests. The try endpoint tests a rule but is not a reviewed proposal.

main_count.reason: Answers (112) and routing rules (41) are nearly all requests.

kinds.label: routing rules
kinds.reason: Leads change rules in the admin page, with checks, history and undo.

kinds.label: answers
kinds.reason: Leads change answers in the admin page, with checks, history and undo.

kinds.label: greeting and opening hours
kinds.reason: Leads change them in the admin page but cannot undo: a path with no undo is reach 0.

kinds.label: queues
kinds.reason: A new queue is a config file edit and a release.

request.reason: Both main kinds are self-serve with undo and GOV-05 is 2; no AI lane or intake for L2.

fix.reason: Self-serve main kinds, rollback at 2 and failed lookups recorded (LRN-03 2); no diagnosis or product build path for L2.

expansion.reason: EXP-02 is excluded for a focused application and DEL-04 is 0, so no build path.
